text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementAstronomy“It Feels Like Something Out of Science Fiction”: Astronomers Find First Green StarThe universe just got a little more colorfulJCBy Jake Currie4:00 PM CDT on October 19, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleOne day, our sun will collapse into a superdense object about the size of Earth—a white dwarf. While our sun is an orangish-yellow, the resulting white dwarf will be… white obviously, right? Not necessarily. According to a new study from the University of Warwick, white dwarfs actually come in a rainbow of different colors.Powered By 10 ShareNextStayThe color of most stars is a function of its temperature: red stars are the coolest, orange and yellow stars are hotter, and blue and white stars are the hottest of all. “Most stars, including most white dwarfs, behave like ‘perfect radiators,’ so their color is set almost entirely by temperature,” study author and astrophysicist Mark Hollands explained in a statement. “But nobody had really looked into what else might be possible for white dwarfs.”Read more: “Did Astronomers Finally Witness a Black Hole Eat a White Dwarf for the First Time?”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
